attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter essay, written in his authorial voice.

semantics.note: In context, 'They' means the AI industry. 'Nor will they ever' is an unhedged, open-ended negative forecast. The present-tense clause is reasonably folded into the forecast.

contract.note: The plain reading (broad independent intellectual task performance with little supervision) is an ordinary, fair reading that is not stretched either way. A narrower reading counting bounded autonomy would face contrary evidence, so the interpretation matters.

evidence.note: ARC Prize, 3 Sep 2026: GPT-6 Astra beats the human efficiency baseline on ARC-AGI-3. These are bounded, deterministic game environments, so this does not show broad intellectual autonomy.
METR testimony, 30 Sep 2026: agents coordinated multi-day autonomous action in a cybersecurity incident. This is real autonomy but within one domain, not verified broad autonomy.
METR, 22 Sep 2026: Claude Opus 5.5 has qualitative weaknesses and is unlikely to fully automate AI R&D. This does not prove the claim that the industry never will.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended forecast that the industry will never succeed. Current shortcomings cannot support it, and no item shows independently verified broad intellectual autonomy that would meet the contradiction condition. e1 and e2 show substantial but bounded autonomy, and e3 shows remaining weaknesses. The evidence does not settle the outcome.
